title: Open Doors, Zero Restraints: How Trieste, Geel & Civilian Crisis Teams Replaced Locked Wards with Belonging
tagline: Ending the false choice between locked psychiatric jails and sidewalk abandonment through Trieste's 24/7 open-door cooperatives, Geel's 700-year host families, unarmed STAR/CAHOOTS vans, and gentle prodromal AI.
cynicBelief: Societies face a grim, unchangeable binary for severe mental illness: either lock people inside coercive psychiatric asylums and county jails with mechanical restraints, or abandon them to sidewalks, subway platforms, and tragic armed police 911 encounters.
breakthroughCounter: Following Franco Basaglia's reform and Law 180 (1978), WHO Collaborating Centre Trieste completely closed its 1,200-bed asylum and shifted 94% of its mental health budget into 24/7 open-door neighborhood centers, housing, and union-wage Type-B social cooperatives—achieving 0% mechanical restraints, near-zero chronic psychiatric homelessness, and a ~40% suicide drop for just ~€77–€79 per capita. Meanwhile, Geel, Belgium has welcomed adults with schizophrenia as family 'boarders' for 700+ years, and Eugene's CAHOOTS plus Denver's STAR unarmed vans cut subsequent minor offenses ~34% (Stanford SIEPR) without arrests or force.
socialNormShift: Cities redirect institutional jail-and-ward spending into 24/7 open-door neighborhood hospitality centers, union-wage social cooperatives, Geel-style nurse-backed host families, and unarmed 911 medic-clinician vans—augmented by opt-in on-device sleep/voice prodromal alerts, metabolic neuro-psychiatry, and ambient scribes so gentle kitchen-table care arrives days before crisis.

humanStory.protagonist: Matteo Furlan (29, Barista-Roaster at Il Posto delle Fragole Co-op) & Hendrick Peeters (Geel Host-Family Baker)
humanStory.location: Trieste, Italy, Geel, Belgium & Denver, Colorado
humanStory.snippet: When Matteo's opt-in phone sleep-rhythm monitor flags three nights of 3:00 AM manic fragmentation, his neighborhood Barcola open-door nurse drops by over espresso four days before a 911 crisis can erupt—adjusting his metabolic anti-inflammatory regimen while keeping Matteo's union barista job, apartment, and dignity 100% intact with zero locked doors.

quote.text: When we unlocked the asylum gates in Trieste, we learned that freedom itself is therapeutic: if you surround a person in crisis with an open neighborhood door, a home, a real paycheck in a social cooperative, and human respect rather than leather straps, society becomes safer and kinder at lower cost.
